contribution: Emperor Justinian ruled the Byzantine Empire (527-565 CE), commissioning the Corpus Juris Civilis (Corpus of Civil Law), building the Hagia Sophia, and attempting to reconquer the western Roman territories lost to Germanic invasions. His reign was marked by the devastating Plague of Justinian.
historical_significance: Justinian's legal reforms preserved Roman law and influenced European legal systems for centuries, his architectural achievements represented Byzantine artistic mastery, and his military campaigns attempted to restore Roman greatness.
